 Order

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of anticipatory bail relating to FIR No.729/2023 dated 14.08.2023, registered at Police Station - Kareli, District Narsinghpur (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Section 420 and 409 of IPC.
Applicant apprehending his arrest in the aforesaid offence has knocked the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. As per prosecution story, on 17.02.2023 applicant Vijay Kushwaha a customer of bank gave Rs.

sentences.text: As per the allegations, he deposited only Rs.70,000/- in the bank in place of Rs. 1,50,000/-.

A complaint was made, in the inquiry it was found that on the date of incident, the complainant had gone to the bank, but there is no proof that he had given Rs.1,50,000/- to the Branch Manager in the Chamber.

Rs.70,000/- were deposited in the bank through deposit form, but after some time as FIR was registered for commission of the offences alleging that the present applicant who was the Chief Manager of the Bank has embezzled Rs.80,000/- by not depositing the same in the bank account of the complainant's father.
3.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the applicant has not committed any offence.
He has been falsely implicated.
He is a bank employee.
Only Rs.70,000/- was deposited by the applicant in the account which is apparent from the receipt of the amount deposited in the account.
The complainant had given only Rs.70,000/- and the same was deposited in his father's account.
FIR has been registered against the applicant due to political intervention, no offence under Section 420 and 409 of IPC is made out.
Applicant has no criminal background.
Therefore, it is prayed that the applicant who is a regular employee of the Union Bank of India may be released on bail.
4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the objector as well as learned Panel Lawyer for the respondent/State has opposed the prayer for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant.

5. Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case but without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which applicant/accused who is a bank employee may be released on anticipatory bail.
Consequently, this anticipatory bail application is allowed.

6. It is directed that in the event of arrest applicant - Arvind Kumar Arya be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Authority.

(iii) Applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;

(iv) In case, applicant is not arrested within a period of 10 days' by the Investigation Officer, he shall surrender himself before the Investigation Officer within 7 days'
from today failing which this order shall become ineffective.
